newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Sphinx sees modest full-year profit.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Sphinx sees modest full-year profit.

text.p: Sanitaryware maker Sphinx said on Thursday it expected to see an improvement in results over the next six months of the current fiscal year, leading to a modest full-year profit.

"Based on the current earnings trend we expect a measure of improvement in results over the second half of the current 1996/97 financial year and a modest profit from ordinary operations over the full year," Sphinx said in a statement.
The firm earlier announced a 2.4 million guilder loss over the 1996/97 first half ended September 30.
Sphinx said the outlook on its markets remained poor, with France and Germany expected to show no improvement in the foreseeable future.
"As such, an improvement in profits will have to come from internal restructuring and cost-cutting measures," it said.

But it said that restructuring measures currently being implemented would only begin to filter through into results in the 1997/98 financial year and more restructuring was needed to ensure long-term profitability, it said.
"In order to achieve an attractive level of profitability again in the long-term additional strategic adjustments will probably be necessary," Sphinx said.
It said the company had to put its finances on a more sound footing by reducing working capital further and divesting certain activities.
